$comment: Canonical wire lines. Each must decode into the named envelope and re-encode to these exact bytes: that is what pins field names, camel casing, which absent fields are omitted and which are written as null. Generated from the Rust types, never by hand.

cases.name: request/claim
cases.why: The shape every shell sends to take the lease. Absent payload fields are omitted, never sent as null.

cases.name: request/sample
cases.why: A confirmed sample. `sequence` and `marker` ride in the same payload object as the owner.

cases.name: request/no-payload
cases.why: A command with nothing to say still sends `payload` as an empty object rather than omitting it.

cases.name: response/state
cases.why: A success carries `error` as an explicit null, and `accountId` inside the state is explicitly null when absent. A client that expects those keys to be missing will not parse this.

cases.name: response/sample-accepted
cases.why: The acknowledgement of a sample. `payload` holds only what the command answers.

cases.name: response/owner-conflict
cases.why: A second owner asking for a lease somebody else holds.

cases.name: response/stale-generation
cases.why: A request scoped to a generation the authority has moved past.

cases.name: response/non-monotonic-sample
cases.why: A sample whose sequence did not advance. Rust refuses it; a shell must not treat the refusal as a transport failure.

cases.name: event/sample
cases.why: The notification envelope. It shares the version and state fields with a response on purpose.
